openings.claim: Shared picking creates interference and omissions; local, pre-counted small batches may improve complete-kit assembly. O4 supports investigating this, not a verified intervention.
openings.delta: Give each volunteer a separate area with materials for a short batch; compare counted contents with the pattern sample before closing envelopes.
openings.prediction: With pattern mixture held constant, local batches produce fewer crossings and picking omissions, with enough time saved to absorb checking.
openings.rival_prediction: O4 used easier patterns: matching the mixture removes its accuracy and speed advantage despite fewer crossings.
openings.defeat: Matched local batches reduce crossings but leave picking omissions and checked assembly time unchanged or worse.
openings.probe: Within one two-volunteer, 90-minute assembly attempt, compare matched short blocks using shared trays versus local pre-counted materials. Record picking discrepancies before filling, filling discrepancies before closure, crossings, and elapsed time. Measure occupied area before staging. Stop the comparison early enough to complete remaining kits and checks; assess all 60 against the stated success measure.
assumptions: Local staged materials fit the existing table; this is unconfirmed.
The comparison and remaining assembly fit 90 minutes; O4 does not establish this.

openings.claim: An exterior pattern name makes kit identity available at distribution, addressing the stipulated reason for three exchanges; completeness remains a separate requirement.
openings.delta: Write each envelope’s pattern name with an existing pencil and verify contents against that name before closure.
openings.prediction: Correct, legible names allow recipients to select their assigned patterns without exchanges caused by invisible kit identity.
openings.rival_prediction: Assignment or contents mismatch causes exchanges; visible names alone leave those exchanges unchanged.
openings.defeat: Exchanges attributed to unclear identity persist when names are legible, correct, and consulted.
openings.probe: Include naming and verification in the same timed assembly attempt; at distribution tally exchanges and compare recipient assignment, exterior name, and contents. This evaluates the bounded marking probe; the full deadline and correction target remain unproven.
assumptions: Recipients’ assigned patterns are accessible during distribution.
Naming and verification time can be accommodated within the assembly limit; measure it.
